title: Assessing the liquidity preparedness of investment funds to meet margin calls in derivatives markets
summary: ECB staff developed four novel indicators to assess euro area investment fund preparedness for derivatives margin calls, finding that over 15% of open-ended funds and ETFs may be inadequately prepared for plausible spikes in margin calls. Historical data from 2022-2023 shows median ratios of initial margin to cash holdings around 20%, though 20% of bond/mixed-asset funds had ratios exceeding 80% of cash holdings. The analysis highlights pockets of vulnerability similar to conditions observed during March 2020 market turmoil.
key_points: Over 15% of euro area open-ended investment funds and ETFs appear inadequately prepared to cope with plausible spikes in margin calls
Indicator 1 (initial margin to cash ratio): Median ratio of ~20% between Q1 2022 and end of 2023, with 20% of bond/mixed funds and 10% of equity funds having ratios exceeding 80% of cash holdings
Indicator 2 (margin flows to cash ratio): Over 20% of funds had maximum weekly margin flows exceeding 80% of cash holdings; ~25% of bond/mixed funds in Q4 2023 posted margins larger than 80% of cash
Bond market volatility increased following monetary policy tightening in late 2023, driving higher margin call ratios
Median ratio of initial margins to HQLA holdings is low, suggesting overall adequate HQLA buffers exist
Spikes in margin calls can lead to procyclical asset sales, as observed during March 2020 and the September 2022 UK gilt crisis
why_it_matters: This ECB analysis identifies structural vulnerabilities in euro area investment funds' liquidity management for derivatives positions. Funds with insufficient cash buffers relative to margin obligations may be forced into fire sales during market stress, amplifying volatility and potentially transmitting liquidity stress across the financial system. Regulators and risk managers can use these four indicators to identify funds requiring higher cash buffers or more diversified high-quality liquid assets.
macro_context: The analysis connects monetary policy tightening to increased bond market volatility and higher margin call pressures on investment funds, particularly affecting bond and mixed-asset funds in late 2023.
market_structure_context: Directly addresses derivatives market plumbing through analysis of EMIR-reported margin data. Proposes four fund-level indicators: (1) ratio of initial margin stock to cash holdings, (2) ratio of margin flows to cash holdings, (3) ratio of initial margin stock to HQLA holdings, and (4) ratio of margin flows to HQLA holdings. Identifies procyclical risk where margin calls can trigger systemic liquidity stress similar to March 2020 market turmoil and September 2022 UK gilt crisis.
important_numbers: 15%+ of euro area funds inadequately prepared
~20% median ratio of initial margin to cash (2022-2023)
20% of bond/mixed funds with ratios >80% of cash
10% of equity funds with ratios >80% of cash
25% of bond/mixed funds in Q4 2023 posting margins >80% of cash
